---
title: "Correctness"
---

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from _common import LABEL, ORDER, SHORT, jsonl, table, usd

RUN = "2026-11-02-correctness"
s = jsonl(RUN, "samples.jsonl")
summ = jsonl(RUN, "summary.jsonl")
run_date = pd.to_datetime(s.created, utc=True).min().tz_convert("America/Vancouver").date()
base, fixed = s[s.config == "baseline"], s[s.config == "fixed"]
n_q, n_ep = int(base.id.nunique()), int(base.epoch.max())
```

Does the app answer correctly? Each model answers `{python} n_q` questions about the taxi table `{python} n_ep` times. An answer passes when its reply fits the schema, its SQL runs in DuckDB, and the number DuckDB returns matches the reference SQL's number (counts exact, averages and percentages within 1%).

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="47%"}
## Pass rate per model

```{python}
rows = []
for m in ORDER:
    g = base[base.model == m]
    r = summ[(summ.model_id == m) & (summ.config == "baseline")].iloc[0]
    rows.append({"model": SHORT[m].replace(" ", "\u00a0"), "passed": f"{(g.outcome == 'pass').sum()} of {len(g)}",
                 "pass rate": r["pass rate"], "SQL errors": r["SQL errors"],
                 "wrong value": r["value mismatches"], "schema failures": r["schema failures"],
                 f"price, {len(g)} answers": usd(r["cost USD"]), "median latency": f"{r['median latency s']} s"})
table(pd.DataFrame(rows), colalign=["left"] + ["right"] * 7)
```

```{python}
fx = {m: fixed[fixed.model == m] for m in ORDER}
line = ", ".join(f"{LABEL[m].split(' (')[0]} {(g.outcome == 'pass').sum()} of {len(g)}" for m, g in fx.items())
q12 = base[base.id == "q12"]
alt = q12.value_note.fillna("").str.contains("other reading").sum()
```

Most failures are on q12, "What is the average trip length?". The question does not say minutes or miles. The reference reads it as minutes. `{python} int(alt)` of `{python} len(q12)` answers read it as miles, with high confidence and a query that runs. Only the value check catches them.

One vocabulary line in the data description ("trip length" means the duration in minutes) fixes it for the GPT models. Passes on q12 after the fix: `{python} line`.
:::

::: {.column width="53%"}
## One failing question, traced

```{python}
r = q12[(q12.model == "gpt-5.4-nano") & (q12.epoch == 1)].iloc[0]
ref = base[base.id == "q12"].reference.iloc[0]
```

**q12** on GPT-5.4 nano, epoch 1. Reference: `{python} f"{ref:.2f}"` minutes.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("| step | what happened |\n|---|---|")
print(f"| model reply | `sql`: `{r.sql}` |")
print(f"| | `unit`: {r.unit}, `confidence`: {r.confidence} |")
print(f"| | `interpretation`: {r.interpretation} |")
print("| schema check | pass: the reply has all four fields |")
print(f"| SQL runs | pass: DuckDB returned {r.value:.2f} |")
print(f"| value check | fail: {r.value:.2f} is not within 1% of {ref:.2f} |")
print(f"| outcome | **{r.outcome}**, {r.tokens_in:,} tokens in, {r.tokens_out} out, {r.latency_s} s |")
```

The model answered a different question well. The `unit` field says which one. A scorer that only checks that the SQL runs would count this answer as correct.
